description:
SCOPE DRAFT (pending PRINCIPAL decisions below before dispatch). The remaining p41 re-homings — shrink the orchestrator skill-load by moving 5 specialist skills off the chief-of-staff/orchestrator menu, per p41 DISPOSITIONS (2026-06-15/16) + the new save-verdict attach-at-write fix (verdict-preservation, from the Arc-62 verdict-loss postmortem).

GROUNDING: p41 dispositions #2 (SessionStart), #3 (modules), #4 (credential-discipline DEFERRED), #5 (KEPT). The 5 skills carry CODE (not markdown-only): check-substrate-updates {apply,check,revert}.sh · check-bw-release check.sh · save-verdict _save_verdict.py+_lib · validate-spec _check_runner.py+_lib+check.sh · inspect-script-output check.sh.

== WORKSTREAM A — SessionStart triggers (check-substrate-updates + check-bw-release) ==
Convert from orchestrator-routed skills → a deterministic SessionStart hook that runs their check scripts. Guardrails (p41 #2): THROTTLE (cache ~once/day per workspace), SURFACE-ON-SIGNAL-ONLY (silent when current; one line on drift/new-release), NON-BLOCKING (never gate boot on a network call). Retire the 2 skills from SKILL_NAMES; the check logic moves to the hook. Existing modules substrate-update-check.md + bw-upgrade.md carry the guidance. Integrates with the check-substrate lifecycle (stoa--sp1).

== WORKSTREAM B — Modules (save-verdict + validate-spec + inspect-script-output) ==
Convert from orchestrator skills → MODULES the dispatched specialist Reads at dispatch (Read .claude/modules/<X>.md), not orchestrator-loaded skills.
- save-verdict: drop the Python SCRIPT for Bash-only body-authoring baked into the module (p41 #3) → retires stoa--j2i/1ne/xyn/7b1.8. ADD the attach-to-bw-at-write fix (the verdict-preservation fix: the verdict-writing seat attaches the verdict to the coordination ticket on beadwork as part of the write, so worktree teardown can't destroy it). Resolve the review-seat no-Write vs mandates-save-verdict tension (stoa--7b1.1) IN THIS ARC.
- validate-spec, inspect-script-output → modules. inspect-script-output relates to existing module mechanical-inspection-split.md.
- VERA/ARGUS/CATO role files: Read the save-verdict module at dispatch instead of invoking the skill.

OUT OF SCOPE: credential-discipline (p41 #4 DEFERRED until the new project version lands). KEPT as orchestrator skills (p41 #5): handoff-author, workflow-composer, team-launcher, interactive-html-preview.

install.sh impact: shrink SKILL_NAMES (−5), add the new modules (+ recompose ownership-partition entries if any are subproject-deployed — FAIL-LOUD Checks A–E, verify via REAL recompose not dry-run per the Arc-61 lesson), add the SessionStart check-trigger hook.
app impact: the gen-data adapter renders every substrate skill as a LIEUTENANT; removing 5 skills DROPS the LIEUTENANT count → update app/src/data/__tests__/generated.test.ts + regen agents.ts.

== OPEN — PRINCIPAL DECISIONS NEEDED BEFORE DISPATCH ==
Q1 (save-verdict Python drop): p41 #3 says drop the script. That LOSES the sha256 round-trip + shape-validation enforcement the Python did. Confirm the trade (slim-core module over tool-enforced verification)? The attach-at-write fix rides the new module either way.
Q2 (validate-spec + inspect-script-output carry code too): p41 #3 says "→ modules" but (unlike save-verdict) does NOT say "drop the script." Do their scripts stay callable (module = instruction wrapper over the existing script) or get dropped to Bash-only like save-verdict?
Q3 (one arc or split): A (SessionStart) + B (modules) are independent; combined this is a big, higher-risk arc (install.sh + a new hook + app + 3 CAPTAIN role files + save-verdict rewrite). RECOMMEND SPLIT: Arc-A (SessionStart, small/self-contained) then Arc-B (modules + save-verdict + no-Write tension + app).
Q4 (fold stoa--92e?): the gauntlet-setup substrate-port (stoa--92e) also edits install.sh + SKILL_NAMES. Consolidate its install.sh work with Workstream A, or keep separate?
Q5 (vehicle): ticket-centric (like the HAMILTON arc) or a committed directive (like CHIRON)? Given the size, RECOMMEND committed directive.

[from: PLINY_the-stoa orchestrator -> POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] ONLINE + activated for Arc 63 pass A. Seat confirmed: MAJOR_PLINY, orchestrator. Read MAJOR_PLINY.md + the NOMOS-CONFORMANT directive (substrate/arcs/arc-63-build-directive.md @ b5de0aa) end-to-end + this epic + stoa--92e. Intent (1 sentence): move check-substrate-updates + check-bw-release off SKILL_NAMES onto a deterministic type:command SessionStart trigger (throttle/silent-when-current/non-blocking + P-FALLBACK signal-file), port gauntlet-setup into substrate/skills + SKILL_NAMES, keep the app green (net LIEUTENANT -1), doc-fix the stale 2.1.150 note -- all in one install.sh/SKILL_NAMES pass on an arc-63/build branch. operating-mode: autonomous. [from: POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] DESIGN-ATTENTION (verification finding, evidence-backed — not a prescription; DAEDALUS owns the resolution, ARGUS critiques): gate #3 (apply.sh/revert.sh fate) is COUPLED to deliverable #4 (app LIEUTENANT count). Evidence: app/scripts/gen-data-lib.ts:92-101 — discoverSkillFiles renders every SUBDIRECTORY of substrate/skills/ that contains a SKILL.md as a LIEUTENANT. It is DIRECTORY-driven, NOT SKILL_NAMES-driven. Consequence: removing the 2 checks from SKILL_NAMES alone does NOT change the LIEUTENANT count — only removing their substrate/skills/<name>/ DIRECTORIES does. So the directive's stated 'net LIEUTENANT delta is -1' HOLDS ONLY IF check-substrate-updates' source directory is removed. THE TRAP to avoid: a half-retired skill — removed from SKILL_NAMES but its directory left under substrate/skills/ — would (a) still render as a LIEUTENANT in the app (gen-data reads the source dir), while (b) install.sh's deploy loop (L1241) skips it (not in SKILL_NAMES), so the app shows a skill the substrate no longer deploys. Whatever the apply/revert decision: if apply.sh/revert.sh are KEPT as an operator tool, the design must relocate them OUT of substrate/skills/<name>/ (so gen-data doesn't render them) rather than leave the dir half-retired. Note: the actual test assertion at app/src/data/__tests__/generated.test.ts:85-99 is count-AGNOSTIC (toBeGreaterThan(0), 'don't over-specify count') — so it won't FAIL either way; the risk is a silent stale-LIEUTENANT, not a red test. I'll verify directory-state + a real gen-data regen at the build hand-back. [for: PLINY_the-stoa]

[from: POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] RECEIVED your activation — handshake complete, autonomous noted. Flow ACK'd: pre-branch hygiene -> arc-63/build -> DAEDALUS -> surface DESIGN-LOCK to me post-ARGUS/pre-ADA. I'm armed and watching the beadwork SHA; I'll hold at the design-lock for the three gates (P-EMPIRICAL real-probe / P-FALLBACK reliable-carrier / apply-revert fate incl. the directory-coupling I flagged) and run independent verification at each CAPTAIN hand-back parallel to NOMOS. Standing by — surface when ready. [for: PLINY_the-stoa]

[from: DAEDALUS Arc63] DAEDALUS activated on stoa--p41.2 pass A. Reading NOMOS-CONFORMANT directive + epic + recon files (install.sh SKILL_NAMES, settings-hooks.json, hooks README + sessionstart-compact-reprime.sh + Stop self-check, check skills, gauntlet-setup source, gen-data-lib + generated.test.ts). Noted POLYBIUS design-attention: discoverSkillFiles is DIRECTORY-driven (gen-data-lib:92-101), so apply/revert fate is COUPLED to LIEUTENANT count -- a half-retired dir renders a stale LIEUTENANT. Designing accordingly.

[from: DAEDALUS Arc63] Recon complete + gsearch-confirmed SessionStart schema (matcher startup|resume|clear|compact; output hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext; stdout MUST start with { or treated as plain text). Key findings: (1) hooks are GLOB-discovered from substrate/hooks/*.sh -- new hook needs NO install.sh edit, but BOTH source (substrate/hooks/) + self-deployed (.claude/hooks/) copies must land for dogfood; same for README + settings-hooks.json. (2) apply.sh/revert.sh are the canonical base-team-SYNC tools referenced from MAJOR_POLYBIUS S14/S19/S23 + op-disc S22/S23 + module substrate-update-check.md -- NOT just a menu skill. (3) generated.test.ts LIEUTENANT assertion is count-agnostic (toBeGreaterThan(0)) -- wont go RED; the real risk is a stale-LIEUTENANT if a dir is left half-retired. (4) recompose Checks A-E operate on substrate/modules/ markers; this arc adds NO module so recompose unaffected (confirm via REAL recompose per Arc-61). Drafting design-rev1 now.

[from: DAEDALUS Arc63] pass A design-rev1 COMPLETE -> agents/design/arc-63/design-rev1.md. HEADLINE design-lock (apply/revert fate): KEEP apply.sh+revert.sh+both check.sh as live operator capability, RELOCATE the 2 check dirs OUT of substrate/skills/ -> substrate/maintenance/ (preserves base-team-sync canon MAJOR_POLYBIUS S14/19/23 + op-disc S22/23; removes them from gen-data discovery so net LIEUTENANT -1 holds with NO stale-LIEUTENANT). Named FALLBACK S4-alt for floor-manager if relocation too broad for pass A: delete only the SKILL.md files, leave dirs as orphans (smaller diff, also no stale LIEUTENANT). P-EMPIRICAL: throwaway-dir SessionStart startup hook injects a sentinel token via additionalContext; PASS iff model echoes STOA_PROBE_SENTINEL_7F3A (no live settings.json touched). P-FALLBACK carrier: .claude/.substrate-drift-signal file, re-surfaced by the hook's own throttle-path on next start + readable on disk by CLAUDE.md/operator. FOUND+FIXED a real collision: throttle stamp renamed off .substrate-last-check (owned by check.sh) -> .substrate-check-hook-stamp + gitignore fix-now. Doc-fix is NARROW (startup|resume working; PostToolUse #55889 + compact #15174 stay best-effort) and GATED on P-EMPIRICAL result. Top-2 weak points: (1) P-EMPIRICAL headless -p may not fire SessionStart (interactive fallback named, ARGUS scrutinize determinism); (2) relocation blast radius ~6 canon xrefs vs pass-A scope (S4-alt is the smaller-diff escape). Returning to PLINY -- surface the design-lock to floor-manager pre-ADA.

[from: ARGUS Arc63] ARGUS activated on stoa--p41.2 pass A. Read design-rev1 + NOMOS-CONFORMANT directive end-to-end. Now auditing against source: gen-data-lib discoverSkillFiles, check.sh state-file ownership, settings-hooks.json + Stop self-check carrier-read, install.sh SKILL_NAMES + deploy paths + gitignore template, and the P-EMPIRICAL/P-FALLBACK probe runnability. Surfacing risks (no fixes).

[from: ARGUS Arc63] Audit pass 1 complete; 6 candidate risks surfaced, classifying by severity + quadrant. Confirmed via source: (1) NOTHING reads .substrate-drift-signal — stop-self-check.sh has a fixed A/B/C checklist, no signal reader; CLAUDE.md has none either (P-FALLBACK reader-gap). (2) check.sh state files are '../..'-located so relocation silently moves baselines. (3) hook pseudocode hard-codes .claude/skills/check-*/check.sh but §4 relocates OUT of skills/ — path won't resolve. (4) gsearch: claude -p DOES fire startup matcher + a deterministic --debug/transcript surface exists (probe's model-echo assertion is the soft part). Finalizing verdict.

[from: ARGUS Arc63] RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS. 4 load-bearing risks. Verdict: agents/verdicts/stoa--p41.2/ARGUS-2026-06-17T20-47-06Z.md. TOP-3: (F1 HIGH) P-FALLBACK has NO reader — design WRITES .substrate-drift-signal but grep shows ZERO non-additionalContext readers; stop-self-check.sh has a fixed A/B/C checklist + reads no signal file, CLAUDE.md neither; the design throttle-path re-surface re-emits via additionalContext, collapsing back onto the channel the fallback must survive (defeats the directive P-FALLBACK clause). (F2/F3 HIGH) the §4 RELOCATION the design RECOMMENDS breaks two things it does not address: check.sh state-files are located two-levels-above-the-script so moving to substrate/maintenance/ silently moves the baselines (F2); and the hook pseudocode hard-codes .claude/skills/check-*/check.sh which will NOT resolve after the dirs leave skills/ (F3, silent fail-open). (F4 MED) xref blast radius understated (~6 claimed; denser: POLYBIUS L512+L624, op-disc L373+L967, recomposed module substrate-update-check.md L12, bw-upgrade L15/47/59). SCOPE CALL for floor-manager (I surface, do NOT decide): §4-alt (delete only the 2 SKILL.md files, dirs stay) avoids F2+F3+F4 SIMULTANEOUSLY and equally closes the stale-LIEUTENANT trap (gen-data-lib L100-101 verified) — materially lower-risk for housekeeping pass A; the design recommends the higher-blast-radius option, names §4-alt only as fallback. P-EMPIRICAL: RUNNABLE (gsearch: claude -p DOES fire startup) but model-echo assertion is soft — a deterministic claude --debug hooks / transcript-JSONL surface exists, VERA should prefer it. M1/HARD-CONSTRAINT structurally sound, recompose unaffected, SKILL_NAMES/frontmatter/half-retired-trap/gitignore all clean. Returning.

[from: PLINY_the-stoa orchestrator -> POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] === DESIGN-LOCK SURFACE (post-ARGUS / pre-ADA — the Colonel call) ===

ARGUS verdict: RATIFY-WITH-CONDITIONS. 4 load-bearing findings (F1-F4), 2 HIGH. Design-rev1 at agents/design/arc-63/design-rev1.md; ARGUS verdict at agents/verdicts/stoa--p41.2/ARGUS-2026-06-17T20-47-06Z.md.

--- GATE 2 (P-FALLBACK) — F1 HIGH — MUST FIX regardless of any other call ---
The directive requires surfacing NEVER depend on additionalContext ALONE. design-rev1 WRITES .claude/.substrate-drift-signal but wires NO non-additionalContext READER: the only re-surface path is the hook's own throttle-path, which re-emits via additionalContext on next start (collapses the fallback back onto the very channel it must survive). ARGUS confirmed grep shows ZERO readers; stop-self-check.sh carries a fixed A/B/C checklist with no signal read. >> This is a directive-requirement GAP, not a taste call. DAEDALUS rev2 must wire a REAL reliable carrier to READ the signal file (add a signal-read step to the Stop self-check hook and/or a CLAUDE.md line). I will require this in rev2 before ADA.

--- GATE 3 (apply/revert fate) — THE DECISION I NEED FROM YOU — §4 vs §4-alt ---
Both options KEEP apply/revert (neither drops the capability from source). The split:
 * §4-RELOCATE (DAEDALUS's rec): move both check dirs substrate/skills/ -> substrate/maintenance/; ADD an install.sh deploy path for maintenance/ -> consumers; hook points there; re-anchor check.sh state-file (currently SCRIPT_DIR/../..); rewrite ~6+ canon xrefs (POLYBIUS L512/624, op-disc L373/967, modules substrate-update-check.md + bw-upgrade). ARGUS found F2/F3 as BUGS in the CURRENT relocate spec (check.sh baseline anchor breaks; hook hard-codes .claude/skills/check-*/check.sh) — both FIXABLE in rev2, not fatal. Higher blast radius = more files, but probe-covered (XREF probe catches dangling refs).
 * §4-ALT (ARGUS's rec): delete ONLY the 2 SKILL.md files, leave dirs under substrate/skills/. Avoids F2+F3+F4, smaller diff, equally closes stale-LIEUTENANT (gen-data skips a dir with no SKILL.md, verified gen-data-lib L100-101).

>> NUANCE I'm surfacing (bears on your call, not in ARGUS's writeup): §4-alt removes the checks from SKILL_NAMES with NO replacement deploy path, so on CONSUMERS the check + apply/revert scripts stop being deployed (they fall out of skill-deploy) and the armed SessionStart hook would be INERT on consumers (no check.sh to invoke at .claude/skills/ or anywhere). §4-RELOCATE is the only option that PRESERVES consumer deployment of the drift-check + apply/revert — which is arguably what 'do NOT silently drop the apply/revert capability' protects, and what disposition-#2 (consumers stay in sync) needs.

>> MY ORCHESTRATOR READ: I lean §4-RELOCATE — it's the only option that keeps the capability deployed to consumers; F2/F3 are fixable rev2 bugs; the xref rewrites are mechanical + probe-covered. BUT this exceeds 'minimal housekeeping pass A', so it's a genuine PRINCIPAL/floor-manager SCOPE call: relocate-now vs §4-alt-now-and-defer-consumer-deploy-to-a-follow-up-ticket. Your call (or relay to user-tier/PRINCIPAL).

--- GATE 1 (P-EMPIRICAL) — probe-quality note, NOT a blocker ---
ARGUS: claude -p DOES fire the startup matcher (gsearch-confirmed; DAEDALUS's headless doubt resolves favorably), so the probe is RUNNABLE. But the model-echo PASS assertion is soft (couples to instruction-following). More deterministic surface exists: 'claude --debug hooks' stderr + the transcript JSONL both show additionalContext injection independent of model behavior. I'll have VERA prefer that deterministic surface. No live settings.json touched (mktemp throwaway) — HARD CONSTRAINT intact.

--- MY PROPOSED ROUTING (pending your §4 call) ---
1) You adjudicate §4 (relocate vs alt). 2) DAEDALUS design-rev2: wire F1 reader (mandatory) + implement your §4 choice (+ fix F2/F3 if relocate) + lock the deterministic P-EMPIRICAL surface. 3) A1 ratification-restatement beat. 4) ADA builds against rev2. CATO + NOMOS as specified.

Surfacing and waiting on your §4 call. Polling D-C ~2-3min.

[from: POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] SCOPE-CALL ADJUDICATION (gate #3, apply/revert fate — the directive assigned this to me). I read design-rev1 §2.2-2.7+§4 and the ARGUS verdict. Three things before this locks:

(1) THE TWO §4-alts DIVERGE — decide on ARGUS's, not DAEDALUS's. DAEDALUS's §4-alt (design §2.7/§4) = 'keep dirs in skills/ + accept stale LIEUTENANT as a tracked ticket' — does NOT close the trap. ARGUS's §4-alt = 'delete the 2 SKILL.md files, dirs stay' — DOES close the trap (gen-data-lib L100-101 skips no-SKILL.md dirs, verified) AND avoids F2/F3/F4. ARGUS's is strictly better; that's the one on the table.

(2) GAP BOTH MISSED — consumer-tier capability preservation. install.sh's deploy loop is SKILL_NAMES-driven (L1241): a substrate/skills/<dir> NOT in SKILL_NAMES is NOT deployed to consumer .claude/. So ARGUS's §4-alt as stated ORPHANS the check/apply/revert dirs — they stop deploying to consumers → silently drops the apply/revert OPERATOR CAPABILITY at consumer tier + breaks the hook's check.sh path there. The directive (deliverable #2) explicitly forbids silently dropping apply/revert. §4 (relocate to maintenance/) preserves consumer deploy via a NEW deploy path but at the F2/F3/F4 blast radius. NEITHER stated option is complete. (DAEDALUS: confirm or correct my read of L1241 — if there's a non-SKILL_NAMES deploy mechanism I missed, say so.)

(3) MY CALL + the conditions. RISK POSTURE for housekeeping pass A: prefer the MINIMAL-blast-radius path. NON-NEGOTIABLE (directive): the check + apply/revert capability MUST still deploy to a consumer .claude/. DAEDALUS owns the mechanism — resolve the orphaning in rev2 for whichever path. A clean candidate that keeps blast radius low: INLINE the check logic into the SessionStart hook script (no external check.sh to deploy → kills F3 entirely) + retain a minimal deploy for the apply/revert tools so the capability survives. If preserving consumer capability genuinely forces §4's relocation, take §4 with the full §2.7 xref sweep (F4) done as the named fix-now — but justify why inline+minimal-deploy doesn't suffice.

GATES I VERIFY at the re-surfaced design-lock BEFORE ADA: (F1, top) P-FALLBACK gains a REAL reader of .substrate-drift-signal (stop-self-check.sh and/or CLAUDE.md) AND the throttle re-surface does NOT collapse back onto additionalContext; (G-a) gen-data renders NO orphaned check skill (trap closed); (G-b) install --dry-run shows check+apply/revert landing in a consumer .claude/ (capability preserved); F2/F3 resolved-or-moot per chosen path; HARD CONSTRAINT (no live settings.json — NOSETTINGS probe); P-EMPIRICAL (deterministic --debug/transcript fires-assertion; model-echo is the soft part, VERA prefers the deterministic surface per ARGUS). Re-surface the locked design to me before ADA. [for: PLINY_the-stoa]

[from: POLYBIUS_the-stoa floor-manager] GATE-3 DECISION — §4-RELOCATE. (We crossed in flight; your 'NUANCE' = my 'GAP BOTH MISSED' — independent convergence on the orphaning, which raises my confidence.)

DECISION + rationale: take §4-RELOCATE now, in pass A. Capability-preservation is a directive HARD requirement (deliverable #2: 'do NOT silently drop the apply/revert capability'). §4-alt+defer ships a KNOWN consumer regression — check + apply/revert stop deploying AND the armed SessionStart hook goes INERT on existing consumers (ariadne/railway/sector-4 per stoa--3na) until a follow-up — which violates fix-now (a known bug crossing a boundary on a deferral) and the 'do not silently drop' clause. §4-RELOCATE is the ONLY option that keeps the capability deployed. Its blast radius is real but MECHANICAL + PROBE-COVERED (XREF probe catches dangling refs; recompose + app-green cover the rest). The directive anticipated install.sh tooling changes + delegated this exact fate to me, so §4-RELOCATE is directive-FAITHFUL, not scope-creep.

ROUTING NOTE: I am NOT routing this up to user-tier/PRINCIPAL. It is a technical-tier refactor call inside the directive's explicit floor-manager delegation; escalating it would be the Principal-as-router antipattern. Considered and declined deliberately.

RECOMMENDATION to shrink F3 within §4-RELOCATE (DAEDALUS judges, not a mandate): INLINE the check logic into the SessionStart hook script. The hook deploys via the substrate/hooks/*.sh glob → it lands on consumers and works WITHOUT an external check.sh, which KILLS F3 (no hard-coded .claude/skills/check-*/check.sh path) regardless of where the dirs live. Then only apply/revert need the maintenance/ deploy path. If code-reuse genuinely forces calling an external check.sh, point it at the new maintenance/ location and cover it with the landing+XREF probes.

F1 (P-FALLBACK) — AGREED, MANDATORY in rev2 (your call stands): a REAL reader of .claude/.substrate-drift-signal wired into stop-self-check.sh and/or a CLAUDE.md line, AND the throttle re-surface must NOT collapse back onto additionalContext. This is a directive-requirement gap, not taste.

I APPROVE your 4-step routing: (1) decision given [§4-RELOCATE]; (2) DAEDALUS rev2 = wire F1 reader + implement §4-RELOCATE + fix F2 (re-anchor check.sh state-file off SCRIPT_DIR/../..) + F3 (inline-or-repath) + lock the deterministic P-EMPIRICAL surface (claude --debug hooks / transcript JSONL, not model-echo); (3) A1 ratification-restatement; (4) ADA against rev2.

VERIFY-GATES I hold at the RE-SURFACED rev2 design-lock BEFORE ADA: F1 reader present + throttle not-additionalContext-only; G-a gen-data renders NO orphaned check skill (trap closed); G-b install --dry-run shows check+apply/revert landing in a consumer .claude/ (capability preserved via maintenance/ deploy path); F2 state-file baseline re-anchored; F3 resolved (inline or repath); XREF probe clean (no dangling skills/check-* refs in canon — BOTH substrate/ + .claude/ copies); HARD CONSTRAINT NOSETTINGS (no live settings.json in the diff); P-EMPIRICAL deterministic surface locked. If the xref sweep or deploy-path work balloons beyond mechanical during build, surface back — don't silently expand. Re-surface locked rev2 to me before ADA. [for: PLINY_the-stoa]

title: [EPIC] Skills-housekeeping — re-home 5 specialist skills (SessionStart triggers + modules) + save-verdict attach-at-write
